review_manifest.json.description: Pinned scope, evidence identities, findings, limitations, and change policy; deliberately omits its own identity

positive_findings: R96 repairs the failed R95 release boundary with a source-first remote lineage, successful workflow, clean reconstruction, and 445 passing tests.
The recursive-risk qualification, centered-risk identity, and risk-specific transport account form a coherent theorem chain under the written assumptions.
The convex-order AVaR enclosure supplies a useful second-order width and a stated sharpness example for the specified midpoint/endpoint bracket.
The sample size, deterministic enclosure allowance, simultaneous family, and equivalence margin are fixed prospectively.
Quadratic, ReLU, and spline continuations receive the same labels, design rank, and serialized payload.
Original-law admission and protected fallback are executed for every proposed service action.
All 32768 arm-state rows are retained and the release recomputes the complete statistical catalogue.
All twelve paired comparisons establish equivalence at the declared margin with the largest half-width about 31.4 percent of that margin.
blocking_findings: The successful certificate, fallback, and recursive guarantee are representation-neutral; R96 does not identify a neural-specific numerical advantage.
The equal-rank quadratic service is fastest at both risk levels, has zero first-proposal rejections, and is statistically equivalent in policy cost.
The manuscript does not sufficiently isolate the novelty of the AVaR rate and constant from classical convexity, quadrature, and tail-risk ingredients.
All twelve policy-cost intervals contain zero, and point estimates favor the online solver; the result is equivalence rather than economic improvement.
The purchase theorem is not instantiated with complete per-arm acquisition costs, a predeclared reuse horizon, or certified break-even price-fee regions.
ReLU and spline first proposals are rejected in roughly 26 to 31 percent of states, so service reliability principally demonstrates verifier resilience.
The active risk experiment remains two-dimensional, two-date, and scalar-control; product quadrature retains a Cartesian point burden and no largest-vector execution is in the release.
Independent verification recomputes statistics but audits only 64 random endpoints and does not independently replay conventional proposal selection or the full learning-to-action stack.
Timing uses five repetitions with uncontrolled processor frequency, while ARM64 evidence lives on a separate sibling lineage and omits full construction and energy.
The active package remains cumulative and lacks a calibrated economic consequence commensurate with Econometrica.
major_required_changes: Reframe the central contribution as certified stored continuations for recursive-risk dynamic programs and state that qualification is method-neutral.
Establish precisely what is novel in the convex-order AVaR enclosure and limit sharpness claims to the proven rule class unless a broader lower bound is supplied.
Execute a complete per-arm acquisition, validation, serialization, deployment, and reuse frontier with predeclared workloads and price-fee grids.
Compare neural and conventional representations over several matched ranks, feature budgets, and label budgets, including the certificate-aware neural readout as an actual arm.
Decompose accepted proposals, rejected proposals, protected refinement, fallback, endpoint work, and time by state region and arm.
Calibrate the equivalence margin to an economically interpretable object or narrow the claim to numerical engineering precision.
Add a longer-horizon, multi-control recursive-risk application with explicit operation, memory, quadrature, and descendant-work ledgers.
Independently reimplement continuous-law endpoints, risk evaluation, action lower bounds, acquisition branching, and conventional selection.
Integrate architecture evidence into one pinned release and report operation counts alongside controlled or normalized timings.
Replace the cumulative archive-style active submission with a focused article and supplement, and record visual inspection of final PDFs.

sibling_evidence.assessment: Reviewed as supplementary robustness evidence but not credited to the pinned R96 source branch. It reports bit-identical outputs and the same arm ordering on ARM64, with frequency uncontrolled and no full-construction or energy replication.

limitations: The reviewer did not refit models, rerun the full Bellman campaign, or create new statistical observations.
The review checks the principal theorem chain and frozen execution records at referee level but is not a formal proof-assistant verification of every inherited theorem.
Timing observations are single-environment descriptive evidence and do not establish a hardware-general distribution.
The final remote source lineage is distinct from a separate local R96 export; this report uses only the pinned 32768-row remote chain.
The ARM64 sibling branch is not part of the pinned reviewed commit.
This advisory review is not an Econometric Society editorial decision.
recommendation: Reject in the present form and close the ordinary cumulative revision cycle. A substantially refocused new paper on certified stored continuations and decision-scale risk precision could merit evaluation, but R96 does not establish an Econometrica-level neural-specific numerical contribution or a consequential economic result.
